title: When I read the Bible, it feels like I am there witnessing the moment…
paragraphs: When I read the Bible, it feels like I am there witnessing the moment…
You can feel the silence after disobedience.

The air that once seemed alive with peace now hangs still. The warmth shifts. The light changes. Nothing looks broken — yet everything is. Adam and Eve stand only a few steps away, and I sense the weight settling into their shoulders. Awareness has entered the world… and with it, shame.

It wasn’t thunder.
It wasn’t fire.
It was quiet.

Sin didn’t explode — it hushed the garden. The intimacy that once felt effortless now feels fragile. I imagine the sound of their breathing. The pause before hiding. The ache of realizing something sacred has fractured.
And standing there as a witness, I can’t help but reflect…
How often does my own disobedience begin the same way — not with chaos, but with subtle silence? When has distance from God felt like a quiet shift in the light rather than a loud collapse?
The stillness invites me to examine my heart… not in fear, but in honesty.
What changes in us the moment we step outside obedience? And how quickly does grace begin moving, even then?
